newsitem.title: USA: Consortium invests $50 mln in Shanghai housing.
newsitem.headline: Consortium invests $50 mln in Shanghai housing.

text.p: A consortium of investors said Tuesday that they have invested $50 million to build Shanghai Lakes Executive Community, a planned housing development in the Pudong New Area of Shanghai, China.

The four financial institutions are Bankers Trust New York Corp, H&Q Asia Pacific, an affiliate of Hambrecht & Quist Inc, mutually-held New York Life Insurance Co, and investment funds managed by HSBC Private Equity Management Ltd, a unit of HSBC Holdings Plc.
The housing development will be marketed to the expatriate community of multinational companies doing business in China.

The investment, said the companies, marks one of the first direct real estate investments in China by U.S. pension funds, the source of HSBC's and H&QAP's funds, and the first direct real estate investment in Asia by Bankers Trust.
The total cost of the community, which is located on the East China Sea, 25 minutes east of Shanghai's new central business district, is $500 million.

When completed, it will be an independent community and house approximately 5,000 expatriates. The development will have its own water treatment plant, integrated property management, and hospital, as well as a Shanghai American School, the Shanghai American Club and a Nicklaus signature golf course.

The companies said that because the investment will be leased to multinational corporations seeking to relocate executives to Shanghai, and will have American-style housing, the risks are dramatically lower than usual for an investment in an emerging market.
At the same time, the returns for the investors, they said, are likely to exceed 30 percent on an annualized basis.
The first stage of the community is planned to open in late 1997. The companies said the development will consist of approximately 300 townhouses and 500 fully detached North American-style homes.
